messages: Maya Nguyen: FYI build is failing on the migration guide CI — anchor to `#client-setup` 404s after the redirect PR merged. Sam H: I saw that in CI too. Which page? Maya Nguyen: /guides/migrate/client-setup/ -> redirects to /guides/migrate/client-setup (no trailing slash). The fragment seems dropped during the redirect so linkcheck flags it. Jon P: Ugh. That's the old permalink normalization change. Redirect preserves path but not fragment normally. Did the link originate from an external redirecting page? Maya Nguyen: It was an internal cross-link from /guides/migrate/index.md that used `[Client setup](/guides/migrate/client-setup#client-setup)` Li Wei: Hmm the header on the target page has an emoji in it ("Client setup :sparkles:") which our slugify post-redirect produces as `client-setup-sparkles` in Docusaurus, but MkDocs build used `client-setup`. So after redirect the fragment doesn't match the generated anchor. Sam H: So two issues: redirect drops fragment, and mismatch in slug generation between the two toolchains. Any quick patch? Maya Nguyen: I pushed a small PR to normalize the header id via explicit frontmatter `slug:` on the target page to force `client-setup` — but CI still fails because the redirect step runs before we apply the frontmatter change in the redirected path. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4872 Jon P: Can we instead update the source link to the canonical anchor produced by the current build? That would be a fast fix — change link to `#client-setup-sparkles` until we normalize. Li Wei: I'd prefer normalizing the anchor so readers don't see emojis in URLs. Also the page snippet order changed in the same PR; code sample moved below the heading which changed the first heading slug in the generated TOC and caused further breakage. Maya Nguyen: Good point — the snippet reorder happened because of the MDX include change earlier. Quick diff: ``` - ## Client setup :sparkles: + ## Client setup ``` and add `slug: client-setup` in frontmatter. Sam H: Can docs-bot run linkcheck against the branch preview to confirm? @docs-bot any chance to run linkcheck on the PR preview env? :pray: docs-bot: Running branch-preview linkcheck for PR 4872 — queued. I will post results here when ready. deploy-bot: note: preview site will be available at https://deploy-preview-4872--docs.redwood.ai/ in ~2m. Jon P: If linkcheck still reports the redirect-fragment drop, we should change the internal cross-link to the full absolute url with the preview host so the redirect preserves fragment? Not ideal but temporary. Li Wei: Absolute preview links are risky. Alternative: add an explicit HTML anchor right above the heading: `` that will ensure the fragment matches regardless of slug behavior. That would be deterministic. Sam H: I like the explicit anchor as a short-term patch. Add it in the PR, run linkcheck, then follow up with slug/frontmatter cleanup in a separate PR to avoid churn. Maya Nguyen: Will add anchor and frontmatter in the PR now. Pushing commit. Maya Nguyen: Commit pushed: added `` and `slug: client-setup` to frontmatter. docs-bot: Linkcheck results for PR 4872 — 2 broken fragments previously, now 0. All other links OK. Sam H: Nice. Can someone file a follow-up ticket to pick a canonical slugify behavior across mkdocs/docusaurus and remove inlined anchors later? Jon P: I'll create a JIRA: DOC-724 — canonical slugify + redirect handling. Assign to eng-docs. Li Wei: Also let's add a short note in the migration guide about MDX include ordering causing heading reflow; saved me 30m. Maya Nguyen: Great teamwork. Leaving the PR open for a codeowner review, but linkcheck green now. :tada:
